A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ClawMachine's visual-token approach to referring and grounding. The main texts, tables, figures, equations and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial changes to the method and organization.

before.justification: v1 reports original region-captioning, visual-grounding and ablation results in Tables 1–7, plus LLaVA-Bench results and qualitative demonstrations in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 reports original results for revised ClawMachine models, including LVIS-Ground, POPE, Ref-Hal, and additional model, encoder and decoder experiments.

M1.justification: v1 uses dynamic token selection and switches between continuous and discrete image features. v2 simultaneously supplies continuous and discrete representations of image patches and trains the projector alongside the LLM during both subsequent stages. Appendix A.5 also extends v1's proposal/GMM decoder with top-3 fuzzy matching, interchangeable proposers and a convex-box fallback. These are procedural changes beyond renaming visual tokens as token collectives.

E1.justification: v2 adds GRIT-20M pretraining, using approximately 15M filtered pairs, and ShareGPT-4V captions. Evaluation expands to LVIS-Ground's multiple-object localization, POPE object hallucination, and the GQA-derived Ref-Hal test of referred attributes and relations. RefCOCO, Visual Genome and LLaVA-Bench coverage is retained; LLaVA-Bench was already evaluated in v1's appendix.

E2.justification: Groma is added to the retained region-captioning, REC and LLaVA-Bench comparisons. The REC comparison also adds UniTAB and Florence-2 (v1 Table 3 versus v2 Table 4). New comparisons include Groundhog in POPE. These additions materially broaden the evaluated comparator set beyond changes to citations or baseline scores.

E3.justification: After the retained projector-alignment step, training changes from image-level conversational learning followed by referential tuning to caption pretraining and joint VQA/referential instruction tuning, with revised data budgets. New protocols include matched-data architecture controls, LVIS top-k recall averaged over ten IoU thresholds, a balanced 1,000-question Ref-Hal test, and latency/FLOPs evaluation. The token-validity metric is removed.

E4.justification: v2 adds controlled comparisons of notation and perception design, alternative visual encoders, and region proposers (Tables 10, 13, 16 and 17). Figure 5 analyzes grounding across object sizes, IoU thresholds and training-data combinations. Hallucination tests and additional qualitative cases broaden the analysis. v1's select-and-merge ablation is removed, while the dual-data study remains in revised form in Appendix A.1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for its experimental results. v2 adds latency averages but does not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v1 Table 1 reports RefCOCOg CIDEr of 106.3 or 112.4 for discrete or continuous inputs; v2 Table 3 reports 115.4 and 118.4 for the revised base and X models. LLaVA-Bench averages change from 83.6 to 87.3. Added results include LVIS-Ground AR of 36.7 and Ref-Hal accuracy of 75.8. These results accompany revised architectures and training, preventing interpretation as controlled same-setting gains.

T1.justification: Equation (1) removes the explicit token-validity definition, the fraction of predicted tokens belonging to the input image. The remaining token precision, recall and IoU definitions are retained. Neither version develops theorems or proofs; the mathematical change is limited to this removed metric definition.

C1.justification: The core claim of unified autoregressive referring and grounding remains. v2 adds hybrid perception, benefits from scaled pretraining, reduced referential hallucination and fast inference as principal contributions. Its abstract also expands the performance claim to scene-level understanding, beyond v1's emphasis on competitive referring and grounding with limited training data.

C2.justification: v2 explains hybrid perception through separate optimization of continuous and discrete embeddings, connects token semantics to small-object grounding, and offers explanations for hallucination differences between methods. Appendix A.5 discusses proposer accuracy/latency tradeoffs, and A.9 adds limitations of segmentation from point prompts. v1's limitations concerning quantization loss and incomplete token generation remain.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands data composition, filtering, initialization and component-training documentation (Tables 11–12 and Appendices A.1–A.2). It adds training durations, detailed Ref-Hal construction and LVIS evaluation instructions, and sampler thresholds and fallback rules. Reported training hardware changes from A800 to A100 GPUs. The project/code URL is retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds substantial positioning against Groma, Groundhog and Florence-2, including an architectural comparison table and Appendix A.4's discussion of representation, optimization and generalization. The tokenization discussion shifts from BEiT, CM3 and DALL-E toward newer autoregressive multimodal work, including Chameleon. The original proxy-versus-geometry taxonomy remains, but its supporting literature and comparative argument are substantially revised.

P1.justification: v2 changes the title and author list and extensively rewrites the introduction and methodological narrative. Experiments are reorganized into referential comprehension, findings and scene-level performance; LLaVA-Bench moves into the main text. The former Appendices A–F become a reorganized Appendix A.1–A.9. This exceeds terminology or formatting edits.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn to show the hybrid feature paths and embedding operations. Grounding and complex-reasoning figures are expanded, while new size/IoU, conceptual and failure-case figures appear. The old training-strategy flowchart is removed. Tables are extensively added and restructured, including replacing the REC average column with training-data information; existing appendix displays are also relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the central design argument: Tables 10 and 16 test perception and notation choices, including controls with identical training data, while Tables 13–15 quantify proposer dependence and computational tradeoffs. LVIS-Ground and Ref-Hal provide quantitative evidence for broader referential behavior, supported by detailed construction and training documentation. Removing token-validity reporting and reducing the dual-data table to prose loses some transparency, but the added controls and evidence provide a clear overall quality gain.
